 Celtics defense gets major test in Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray 
 Boston hasn't allowed a 30-point scorer all season, but facing Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray in Denver will be the ultimate test of their elite defense. By Ben Handler | Nov 18, 2026, 6:45 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Nov 16, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic (15) reacts in the third quarter against the Phoenix Suns at Ball Arena. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Celtics' defense has been extremely impressive so far this season, boasting the second-best defensive rating in the league. They’re holding teams to just 103.3 points per game, which leads the league, and they’re turning teams over and causing chaos frequently, taking away the rim and forcing teams to rely on three-point shooting much more than in years past.
--> The Celtics' defense has been extremely impressive so far this season, boasting the second-best defensive rating in the league. They’re holding teams to just 103.3 points per game, which leads the league, and they’re turning teams over and causing chaos frequently, taking away the rim and forcing teams to rely on three-point shooting much more than in years past.
 They’re also doing a particularly good job honing in on stars and big scorers and containing them. Boston still hasn’t allowed an individual opponent to reach 30 points in a game, and they’ve already done a good job of slowing down Jalen Brunson, Tyrese Maxey, and other elite scorers.
--> They’re also doing a particularly good job honing in on stars and big scorers and containing them. Boston still hasn’t allowed an individual opponent to reach 30 points in a game, and they’ve already done a good job of slowing down Jalen Brunson, Tyrese Maxey, and other elite scorers.
 But on Wednesday night, they’ll get one of their stiffest tests of the season as they face an elite center in Nikola Jokic and an elite scoring guard in Jamal Murray. The Nuggets are always tough in Ball Arena, and they should be angry coming off an ugly loss to the Suns on Monday night as they get ready to host the Celtics on Wednesday night.
--> But on Wednesday night, they’ll get one of their stiffest tests of the season as they face an elite center in Nikola Jokic and an elite scoring guard in Jamal Murray. The Nuggets are always tough in Ball Arena, and they should be angry coming off an ugly loss to the Suns on Monday night as they get ready to host the Celtics on Wednesday night.
 Murray is on a heater, averaging 26.1 points per game this season and shooting over 47% from the three-point line. The Joker’s stats have been down a bit, but he’s still averaging a near triple-double, and he’s unlike any other big man in the league, posing a massive threat to the Celtics’ revamped front line.

The Joker’s stats have been down a bit, but he’s still averaging a near triple-double, and he’s unlike any other big man in the league, posing a massive threat to the Celtics’ revamped front line.
 Celtics haven't faced a threat like the Murray-Jokic combo all season

 Neemias Queta has been an incredible rim protector and deterrent this season, but Jokic is a completely different animal than anything he has faced. Beyond that, Boston was exposed a bit on Monday night as Queta sat out, and the Magic were able to dominate the glass and get anything they wanted inside the paint against Mitchell Robinson and Luka Garza.

Beyond that, Boston was exposed a bit on Monday night as Queta sat out, and the Magic were able to dominate the glass and get anything they wanted inside the paint against Mitchell Robinson and Luka Garza.
 Denver hasn’t been up to their standards so far this season, but their two superstars have still been great, and they’re going to get up for this game. Even with the slow start, they’re 7-5 this season and will surely not take this matchup with the Celtics lightly. The thing is, beyond Murray and Jokic, who are both playing at an All-NBA level, the supporting cast has been extremely pedestrian.

Even with the slow start, they’re 7-5 this season and will surely not take this matchup with the Celtics lightly. The thing is, beyond Murray and Jokic, who are both playing at an All-NBA level, the supporting cast has been extremely pedestrian.
 Aaron Gordon has taken a big step back, Cam Johnson hasn’t stepped up, DeMar DeRozan isn’t the answer, and nobody else can really create a bucket. If - and it’s a big if - the Celtics can handle Jokic and Murray, as they’ve largely been able to with other stars, they should be in great shape and may come out of this litmus test looking very good.

 But if not, this could be a bit of an eye-opener in terms of top-tier star competition that may force the Celtics to reevaluate some things on the roster and with different lineups going forward.
